analysis.one_liner: Makes and sells Tata-brand cars, EVs and CNG vehicles in India and owns Jaguar Land Rover in the UK, after demerging its commercial-vehicle business into a separately listed company in October 2025.
analysis.whats_happening: On 12 October 2026 TMPV signed a technology and platform-sharing agreement with Stellantis for international markets. Q2 FY27 (Sep quarter) volumes were already reported on 3 October: a record 201,723 units sold, up 40% YoY, driven by EVs and CNG. The P&L for that quarter is due around 14 November 2026 - about four weeks out, so not immediate.
analysis.plain_terms: The headline P/E looks almost too cheap to believe (around 1.3-1.5x), and that is the tension: it is not a bargain, it is an accounting illusion from a one-time demerger gain. Strip that gain out and the actual car-and-SUV business was close to breakeven last year. India sales (Tata cars, EVs, CNG) are growing fast and gaining share; the bigger profit engine, Jaguar Land Rover, is under real pressure from China, US tariffs and warranty costs. Both things are true at once.
analysis.quarters: Q1 FY27 (Jun 2026 quarter): revenue up 9.3% YoY to Rs 95,799 crore, but consolidated PAT fell 80% YoY to Rs 775 crore as EBITDA margin slipped to 7.4% (-130bps) and EBIT margin to 2.4% (-90bps). Management blamed a JLR supplier fire, a 25% wholesale decline in China, and higher warranty costs, partly offset by a US tariff cut (27.5% to 10%). FY26 (full year) is where the real distortion sits: consolidated PAT was reported at Rs 82,645 crore, but Rs 82,616 crore of that was a one-off exceptional gain booked on the commercial-vehicle demerger - excluding it, the underlying business was roughly breakeven to a loss, and full-year EBITDA margin had already fallen to 6.8% from 13.4% the year before. Q2 FY27 volumes (reported 3 Oct 2026) hit a record 201,723 units, +40% YoY, but the margin picture for that quarter is not out yet.
analysis.performance_read: The uncomfortable number first: TMPV is down 74.9% from its July 2024 peak of Rs 1,142.47, trading near its 52-week low band. But that headline overstates the damage - in October 2025 the company demerged its commercial-vehicle business 1:1 into a newly listed 'Tata Motors Ltd' (the old CV arm), so every pre-demerger shareholder also received one share of that entity, which trades around Rs 422.8 today. Added back, a holder since the 2024 peak has TMPV (Rs 286.85) plus the CV share (~Rs 422.8) = ~Rs 709.65, versus Rs 1,142.47 at peak - a combined drawdown of roughly 38%, not 75%. Still a real decline, and still far worse than the Nifty, but less than half as bad as the raw chart implies. The supplied 3Y (-55%) and 5Y (-42%) returns on TMPV alone have the same problem - they don't add back the CV shares received - so actual shareholder returns over those periods are also understated, though precise figures can't be reconstructed without the CV entity's full price history. Even adjusted, TMPV has lagged the Nifty (+16.8% 3Y, +25.3% 5Y) and broadly tracked or trailed peer Maruti.
analysis.valuation_read: The reported P/E of roughly 1.3-1.5x is not a signal of cheapness - it is arithmetic noise from the Rs 82,616 crore one-off demerger gain sitting in FY26 earnings, and should be ignored. A more honest yardstick is price-to-book, where TMPV trades close to book value (roughly 0.9-1.0x across most sources, with one 1.3x figure set aside as an outlier) - neither expensive nor a screaming bargain. The low valuation on 'clean' profitability metrics (reported ROE near -1%, ROCE under 1%) looks more like the market pricing in genuine weak near-term earnings at JLR than a market mistake.
analysis.growth_read: Split picture, and it matters which half you're looking at. India passenger vehicles: clearly volume-led growth - Q1 FY27 volumes up 46% YoY, Q2 FY27 sales up 40% YoY to a record 201,723 units, with EVs and CNG now 45% of the mix and EV volumes up 96% YoY. Jaguar Land Rover, which drives most group profit, is volume-declining - China wholesales down 25% - so consolidated revenue growth (+9.3% in Q1 FY27) is coming more from mix/currency than from JLR volumes. The profitable half of the business is currently the shrinking half.
analysis.health_read: Debt-to-equity of about 0.7x looks moderate, but debt-to-EBITDA has risen to roughly 6.5x - not because debt has ballooned, but because EBITDA has compressed sharply as JLR's margins fell. That makes this primarily a business-risk story (China demand, tariffs, warranty costs, the lingering effect of the 2025 JLR cyberattack) rather than a balance-sheet or over-leverage problem; JLR also ran negative free cash flow through FY26 as production normalised after the attack, which is worth watching if margin pressure persists.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoter (Tata Sons) holds 42.51%, essentially flat and with zero pledging - a clean register on that front. Institutional holders are a mix of FIIs (17.11%), mutual funds (10.05%) and insurers (6.47%), with retail at 23.1%. No marquee individual investor stands out in the shareholding pattern - this is an institution-and-retail-held stock, not one with a well-known name on the register.
strengths: India PV volumes up 46% YoY in Q1 FY27 and a record 201,723 units (+40% YoY) in Q2 FY27 sales
EV and CNG now 45% of domestic volume mix; EV sales up 96%+ YoY, giving a hedge against ICE decline
Zero promoter pledging and a stable ~42.5% promoter stake
Trading near book value (P/B ~0.9-1.0x), not priced at a premium despite the India PV growth story
watchpoints: FY26's headline Rs 82,645 crore profit is almost entirely (Rs 82,616 crore) a one-off demerger gain - underlying operations were close to breakeven; don't read the low P/E as cheapness
JLR, the larger profit contributor, faces a 25% China wholesale decline, US tariffs, higher warranty costs and a cyberattack hangover - FY27 EBIT margin guided below 4%
FY26 dividend halved to Rs 3/share from Rs 6 the year before - a visible signal of cash conservatism
Debt-to-EBITDA near 6.5x, elevated because EBITDA has compressed - leverage ratios will keep worsening if JLR margins slip further
analysis.one_thing: JLR's EBIT margin over the next two quarters against its own <4% FY27 guidance - that will show whether the China/tariff/cyberattack hit is bottoming out or still deepening, which decides whether group profit (excluding the demerger gain) actually recovers.
analysis.data_notes: Q1 FY27 PAT (Rs 775 crore, -80% YoY), the Rs 82,616 crore FY26 demerger gain, the dividend cut to Rs 3, and the 1:1 demerger ratio were each corroborated across 2-3 independent sources (Business Standard, Kotak, Business Upturn, HDFC Sky, Upstox). P/B clustered at 0.9-1.0x across most sources; one 1.3x figure was set aside as an outlier. The current price of the demerged CV entity (~Rs 422.8, used only to illustrate the true combined drawdown from peak) came from a single source (Kotak Neo) and is not part of the verified TMPV dataset supplied - treat that combined-return figure as indicative, not exact. Could not verify a precise like-for-like 3Y/5Y total-return figure that accounts for the demerged shares.
